title: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus
summary: Mark opens with the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, citing Isaiah's messenger in the wilderness. John appears baptizing for the remission of sins, clothed in camel's hair, and says one mightier than he is coming who will baptize with the Holy Ghost. Jesus is baptized by John in the Jordan, sees the heavens opened and the Spirit descending like a dove, and hears a voice, 'Thou art my beloved Son.' The Spirit drives him into the wilderness for forty days to be tempted by Satan.

title: Calling the Disciples and Healing in Capernaum
summary: After John is put in prison, Jesus comes to Galilee preaching that the kingdom of God is at hand, and calls Simon and Andrew, then James and John, who leave their nets. In the Capernaum synagogue he teaches with authority and commands an unclean spirit to leave a man. He heals Simon's mother-in-law of a fever, heals many at evening, and prays alone before dawn. A leper begs for cleansing, and Jesus touches and heals him, telling him to say nothing, but the man spreads the news.

title: The Paralytic and Controversies
summary: In Capernaum four men lower a paralyzed man through the roof to Jesus, who forgives his sins; scribes think this blasphemy, and Jesus heals him to show his authority. He calls Levi the tax collector, eats with sinners and says he came to call sinners. Asked why his disciples do not fast, he speaks of the bridegroom, and he defends them plucking grain on the Sabbath. In a synagogue he heals a man's withered hand, and the Pharisees and Herodians plot to destroy him.

title: Parables and Calming the Storm
summary: Teaching from a boat on the Sea of Galilee, Jesus tells the parable of the sower and four soils and explains it to his disciples privately, saying the mystery of the kingdom is given to them. He also teaches about a lamp under a bushel, the seed growing by itself, and the mustard seed. In the evening he crosses the lake; a great storm fills the boat while he sleeps, and the disciples wake him. He rebukes the wind, the sea becomes calm, and they ask in fear who he is.

title: The Gerasene Demoniac, Jairus and the Woman
summary: In the country of the Gadarenes a man with an unclean spirit, who lives among the tombs and breaks chains, meets Jesus; the spirit says its name is Legion and begs to enter a herd of about two thousand swine, which rush into the sea. The man is found clothed and in his right mind. Back across the lake, Jairus asks Jesus to heal his dying daughter; on the way a woman with a twelve-year flow of blood touches his cloak and is healed, and Jesus then raises the girl.

title: Feeding the Multitude
summary: The apostles return and report to Jesus, who takes them to a desert place to rest, but crowds run ahead. Moved by compassion, he teaches them, and as evening comes he takes five loaves and two fish, blesses and breaks them, and the disciples distribute them to about five thousand men; twelve baskets of fragments remain. He sends the disciples across by boat, and in the fourth watch he walks on the sea toward them and says, 'It is I; be not afraid.'

title: Peter's Confession and the Transfiguration
summary: On the way to Caesarea Philippi Jesus asks who people say he is, and Peter answers, 'Thou art the Christ.' Jesus begins to teach that the Son of man must suffer, be killed and rise, rebukes Peter for objecting, and says his followers must take up their cross. Six days later he leads Peter, James and John up a mountain where his clothes turn shining white and Elias and Moses appear. A voice from a cloud says, 'This is my beloved Son: hear him.' He then heals a boy with a dumb spirit.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: As Jesus leaves Jericho with his disciples and a great crowd, blind Bartimaeus, son of Timaeus, sits by the highway begging. Hearing that it is Jesus of Nazareth, he cries out, 'Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.' Many tell him to be quiet, but he cries louder, and Jesus stops and has him called. Bartimaeus throws off his garment and comes. Asked what he wants, he says, 'that I might receive my sight', and Jesus says his faith has made him whole; he sees and follows Jesus.

title: Triumphal Entry and the Temple
summary: Near Jerusalem Jesus sends two disciples for a colt that no one has sat on and rides it into the city while people spread garments and branches and cry 'Hosanna.' He looks around the temple and goes to Bethany. Next day he curses a fig tree with leaves but no fruit, and in the temple drives out those buying and selling, saying it is to be a house of prayer for all nations. The chief priests and scribes seek to destroy him. The fig tree is found withered, and they ask by what authority he acts.

title: The Last Supper and Gethsemane
summary: Two days before Passover the chief priests and scribes seek to take Jesus by craft. At Bethany a woman breaks an alabaster box of costly ointment on his head; some object, but Jesus says she has anointed him for burial. Judas agrees to betray him for money. At the Passover supper Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him and gives them bread and a cup as his body and blood of the covenant. In Gethsemane he prays, 'Abba, Father,' and Judas comes with a crowd and kisses him; Jesus is seized.

title: Trial, Crucifixion and Burial
summary: Jesus is taken to the high priest, where witnesses give conflicting testimony; asked if he is the Christ, he says 'I am' and speaks of the Son of man at the right hand of power, and the council condemns him. Peter denies him three times and weeps when the cock crows. Before Pilate, Jesus says little; Pilate releases Barabbas at the crowd's demand and has Jesus scourged. Soldiers mock him, and he is crucified at Golgotha between two robbers. A centurion says, 'Truly this man was the Son of God.'

title: The Empty Tomb
summary: After the Sabbath, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome buy spices to anoint Jesus' body and come to the tomb very early on the first day, wondering who will roll away the stone. They find it already rolled away and, inside, a young man in a white robe who tells them Jesus of Nazareth has risen, they will see him in Galilee, and Peter should be told. They flee trembling and say nothing to anyone, for they are afraid. Some early manuscripts end here; others add verses 9 to 20.
